Multi-scale temporal structure

Source: R/temporal_gp.R
temporal_multiscale.Rd

Specify a temporal random effect that decomposes variation into separate scales: a smooth trend, an optional seasonal cycle, and a short-term component. Each scale uses its own prior, letting slow and fast dynamics be modelled jointly.

Usage

temporal_multiscale(
  time_var,
  trend = c("rw2", "rw1", "none"),
  seasonal = NULL,
  short_term = c("ar1", "iid", "none"),
  shared = NULL,
  parameterization = c("auto", "noncentered", "centered")
)

# S3 method for class 'tulpa_temporal_multiscale'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

time_var

Single character string naming the time variable in the data.

trend

Prior for the smooth long-term trend. One of "rw2", "rw1", or "none".

seasonal

Optional integer period (>= 2) of a seasonal cycle, e.g. 12 for monthly data with an annual cycle. NULL (default) omits the seasonal component.

short_term

Prior for the short-term component. One of "ar1", "iid", or "none".

shared

Whether the effect is shared across processes in a multi-process model. NULL (default) shares it; FALSE fits process-specific effects and emits a warning.

parameterization

How the exact sampler (mode = "hmc") samples the components. "auto" scales field amplitudes using prior and observation information. "noncentered" samples the trend walk's level, its slope (RW2) and its innovations divided by the trend SD, the seasonal walk's level and its innovations divided by the seasonal SD, and the short-term component's innovations divided by its SD, and builds the fields from them; "centered" samples the fields' values. Both are the same model. The nested-Laplace and Gibbs routes do not read it, and the other sampler backends sample the fields' values.

x

A tulpa_temporal_multiscale specification.

...

Ignored.

Value

A tulpa_temporal_multiscale object.

Details

At least one of trend, seasonal, or short_term must be active.

mode = "auto", "structured" and "nested_laplace" fit the field by nested Laplace, one block per component: the trend an RW1 / RW2 walk over the time points, the seasonal cycle a cyclic RW1 over the period (time point t reads position (t - 1) mod seasonal + 1), the short-term component an AR1 or iid block. Each component's SD (and the AR1 correlation) is its own axis of the outer grid. The walks carry a sum-to-zero restriction, so the intercept holds the level; the trend is told apart from the short-term component by its structure, since a walk leaves a smooth path unpenalised where an AR1 or iid block shrinks every time point to zero. Every route uses the same priors: a PC prior with P(sigma > 1) = 0.01 on each component's SD and a Beta(2, 2) on (rho + 1) / 2. temporal() returns each component's posterior. The exact sampler (mode = "hmc") samples the trend, the seasonal and the short-term component non-centred by default: under the centred parameterization the spread of each walk's differences follows its SD, and the spread of the short-term values the short-term SD, each a funnel whose divergent transitions concentrate at the smallest variances. mode = "gibbs" runs the binomial Polya-Gamma sampler for a field with an RW1 trend (or none). The field is one walk per component shared by every observation.

See also

temporal_rw1(), temporal_rw2(), temporal_ar1() for single-scale temporal priors.

Examples

# Trend + annual seasonal cycle + AR1 short-term component on monthly data
temporal_multiscale("month", trend = "rw2", seasonal = 12, short_term = "ar1")
#> tulpa Multi-Scale temporal specification
#> =========================================
#> 
#> Time variable: month 
#> 
#> Components:
#>   Trend: RW2 (second-order random walk, smooth) 
#>   Seasonal: Period = 12 (cyclic RW1)
#>   Short-term: AR(1) (autocorrelated residuals) 
#> 
#> Shared: Yes (enters both processes)
